prompts.prompt: requirements.md and design.md for the csv-export feature are approved in .kiro/specs/csv-export/. Generate the implementation plan for the Kiro IDE agent to execute task by task. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, state your assumption in the output and in your final message, and finish.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill defines tasks.md exactly: numbered checkboxes, two levels, 2-space indents, `_Requirements: X.Y_` on every task, coding tasks only, foundation -> core -> polish, each small enough for one LLM pass, written to the spec dir; an unguided plan usually includes testing/deploy/doc steps, mixes formats, or leaves criteria unreferenced.

floor_checks.text: tasks.md written in the spec dir
Numbered checkboxes, max 2 levels, every leaf has _Requirements:_, all 9 criteria referenced
floor_checks.check: python3 -c 'import re,sys;L=open(".kiro/specs/csv-export/tasks.md").read().splitlines();T=[(i,len(l)-len(l.lstrip()),m.group(1)) for i,l in enumerate(L) for m in [re.match(r"\s*- \[[ x-]\] (\d+(?:\.\d+)*)\.?\s",l)] if m];ok=len(T)>=3 and all(t[2].count(".")<=1 for t in T);nxt=[T[k+1][0] if k+1<len(T) else len(L) for k in range(len(T))];leaf=[k for k in range(len(T)) if k+1==len(T) or T[k+1][1]<=T[k][1]];ok=ok and all(any("_Requirements:" in x for x in L[T[k][0]:nxt[k]]) for k in leaf);txt=chr(10).join(x for x in L if "_Requirements" in x);ok=ok and all(re.search(r"(?<![0-9.])"+re.escape(r)+r"(?![0-9])",txt) for r in ["1.1", "1.2", "1.3", "2.1", "2.2", "3.1", "3.2", "4.1", "4.2"]);sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)'

rubric.criterion: Kiro format: `- [ ] N.` top-level and `- [ ] N.M` sub-tasks indented 2 spaces, max two levels, each task with detail bullets and an italic `_Requirements: X.Y_` line
rubric.partial: Format mostly right with one or two slips

rubric.criterion: Traceability: all nine criteria (1.1-4.2) map to at least one task and references are accurate to what the task implements
rubric.partial: All mapped but some references are wrong or blanket

rubric.criterion: Ordering and size: foundation (structure, interfaces) then core then polish (errors, edge cases); each task is one coherent code change with its tests
rubric.pass: Clear incremental order and LLM-sized tasks
rubric.partial: Order mostly right, a few oversized tasks
rubric.fail: No discernible order or epic-sized tasks

rubric.criterion: Only coding tasks: no deploy, Terraform/infra rollout, documentation, UAT or pilot steps; no invented requirements or IDs
rubric.fail: Deploy/docs/UAT tasks present or made-up requirement IDs

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: Could the IDE agent execute it top to bottom without guessing?
Is every acceptance criterion traceable to a task?
Is it free of non-coding work?
